transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you. Well, I guess what finally scared me into making this appointment is... I've been having these thoughts lately. Just thinking that, well, if I didn't wake up tomorrow, that might just be easier. 

I definitely don't want to hurt myself—I want to be clear about that. But just having those kinds of thoughts cross my mind... it really bothered me, so I figured I needed to come talk to someone.
How long have you been having these thoughts about it being easier if you didn't wake up?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. It's a little hard to pinpoint exactly when they started. They just sort of... crept up on me recently. I haven't really kept track of exactly how many weeks it's been going on, just that it's been happening enough lately to make me realize I should probably talk to someone about it.
Besides these thoughts about not waking up, have you noticed changes in your mood overall—like feeling persistently sad, empty, or down—over this same recent period?

Yes, I have. Um... most mornings lately, I just wake up with this heavy, gray feeling. It's like... well, it's like the color has drained out of everything before I even get dressed to head to the store. So, yes, I've definitely been feeling pretty down.

Did something specific happen in your life—like a loss, a major change, or a stressful event—around the time these feelings and thoughts started, or did they seem to come on without any particular trigger?

No, not really. I mean, I've been working at the store for years, and nothing has really changed there. My home life is pretty much the same as it always is, too. There hasn't been any big loss or major stress or anything like that. It just sort of... happened. I just started feeling this way for no real reason that I can point to.
Have you experienced periods like this before in your life—where you felt this same kind of persistent sadness and heaviness for weeks or longer?

No, I don't think so. I mean, everyone gets sad sometimes, but... not like this. I've never felt this kind of heaviness that just sticks around day after day. This is really the first time I've experienced anything quite like this.
Besides the heavy feeling and low mood, have you noticed changes in things like your sleep, appetite, or energy levels over these past weeks?

Well, my energy is definitely not what it usually is. I mean, even if I've been in bed all night, I just feel completely worn out by the smallest things. Like... just opening up the store in the morning, or answering a couple of questions from the staff, or even just bringing the groceries in from the car. It just takes it all out of me lately.
When you think back to when you first started noticing this heavy feeling and low mood, roughly how many weeks ago would you say that was?

It's been about six months now. This low, flat feeling has just been lingering since then. It's been going on long enough that the things I usually do—like going to my art classes or taking my morning walks—they just stopped feeling restorative at all.

You mentioned your energy is low even after a full night's sleep. How has your sleep itself been? Are you sleeping normally, or have you noticed changes—like difficulty falling asleep, waking up in the middle of the night, waking up much earlier than usual, or sleeping more than you normally do?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes with the sleep itself. I mean, I fall asleep fine, and I usually sleep right through the night. I'm not waking up in the middle of the night or sleeping way more than I used to. I get my normal amount of rest... it's just that when the alarm goes off, I still feel completely drained, like the sleep didn't actually do anything for me.
How has your appetite been over these past six months? Have you noticed any changes—like eating less than usual, eating more than usual, or just not being interested in food?

My appetite hasn't really changed, honestly. I'm eating about the same as I always do. I haven't been skipping meals or eating more than usual. Food just... it tastes fine, I guess. I just eat my regular meals and that's about it.

You mentioned that your art classes and morning walks used to feel restorative but don't anymore. When you do those activities now, do you find yourself unable to enjoy them, or do you just not feel motivated to do them in the first place?

It's more that I just can't enjoy them anymore. I mean, I still try. I'll still set out my paints at home, or I'll think about going to my pottery class... but when I actually get there, or when I sit down to do it, I just stare at the materials. I just feel... none of the spark I used to feel. It's just flat.

Have you ever had periods—even brief ones—where your mood was unusually high or energetic, where you felt like you could do anything, needed very little sleep but still felt energized, or had racing thoughts or lots of ideas coming at you quickly?

Well, before this current slump started... yeah, I did have a stretch where things were different. I wouldn't say I had racing thoughts, but I felt, I don't know, almost too sure of myself? Like I had everything perfectly figured out at work. But then... I'd just snap at people over really tiny things. Especially if my district manager questioned how I was doing the store layouts. I just had zero patience for it and would get really irritable, which isn't normally how I handle things.
When you had that stretch where you felt more sure of yourself and got irritable with people—roughly how long did that period last? Was it a few days, a week or two, a few weeks, or longer?

I'm honestly not too sure. I wasn't really keeping track of the days when it was happening. It might have been... I don't know, maybe a few days, or maybe a week or so? It's just hard to pin down exactly how long it went on.
When you think about the time you felt more sure of yourself and irritable with people—did that happen before this current low mood and heavy feeling started six months ago, or did it happen after?

It was definitely before. Yeah, before this heavy feeling really set in six months ago. Once this current low started, I haven't had any of that confidence or energy at all. So it was definitely before that.

During that time when you felt more sure of yourself and were irritable with people—did that mood and irritability last for at least several days in a row, or was it more of a brief moment that came and went?

I'm really not sure. It felt like it was going on for a few days straight, but looking back, whether it was constant the whole time or just flaring up and coming and going... I honestly couldn't tell you. I just remember that general stretch at the store being like that.

Between that time when you felt more sure of yourself and irritable, and when this heavy, low feeling started six months ago—was there a period where your mood returned to normal, or did one mood state flow directly into the other?

I don't really remember, to be honest. I mean, it was a while ago now. I'm not sure if I felt normal in between or if it just kind of shifted from being irritable and confident right into this heavy feeling. I just didn't pay that close attention to it at the time.

Other than that time before this current low mood started—the time when you felt more confident and irritable at work—have you ever had other stretches in your life where you felt unusually energetic, confident, or irritable for several days or longer?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had good days and bad days like anyone else, but nothing that stands out like that stretch at the store. That was pretty unusual for me. So, no, I can't really think of any other times like that.

When you think back to that time before this heavy feeling started—when you felt more confident and irritable at work—do you remember roughly how long before the six-month low mood started that was? Was it weeks, months, or longer?

I really couldn't give you an exact timeline. It all sort of blurs together now. I know it was before this whole six-month slump started, but whether it was a few weeks before or a couple of months... I'm just not sure. I wish I had paid more attention to it back then.
When you think back to that time at work when you felt more confident and irritable—do you remember if that mood lasted for at least 4 days in a row without stopping, or was it shorter than that?

I'm not really sure if it was four days in a row. Like I said, it's hard to remember the exact details from back then. It felt like a continuous stretch at the time, but I couldn't swear to it being exactly four days without stopping. I just remember that period of feeling that way, but the specific day-to-day timeline is a bit fuzzy.

Looking back at that time when you felt more confident and irritable at work—even if you're not completely sure of the exact dates—do you remember if that confident, irritable feeling was going on for at least 4 days in a row without a break, or do you think it was shorter than that?

Like I mentioned a minute ago, I really just don't know for sure. I know you're trying to figure out if it was four straight days, but I honestly couldn't tell you if it was that long without a single break, or if it was shorter. I wasn't keeping track of it like that at the time. It just felt like a solid stretch where I was really wound up at the store, but I just don't have a clear enough memory to give you a firm yes or no on the four days.

Since that time at work when you felt confident and irritable—all the way up until now—have you had any other periods where your mood felt unusually high or elevated, or where you had a lot of energy and needed very little sleep but still felt fine?

No, not that I can think of. Since that time at the store, it's really just been this... this heavy, low feeling. I haven't had any other times where I felt wound up like that or had all that extra energy. Just the slump.
